title: Manual GPT-5.4 selection falls back to another model and does not return automatically
body:
Type: Bug 1. Open VS Code and start a new GitHub Copilot Chat conversation. 2. Manually select GPT-5.4 as the chat model. 3. Ask several questions in the same conversation. 4. At some point, the conversation appears to fall back to an older/weaker model. 5. Continue using the same conversation and observe that it does not automatically return to GPT-5.4. Actual result: Even though I manually selected GPT-5.4, the conversation appears to switch to another model and stay there. After that happens, response quality noticeably degrades. I can usually tell because the assistant starts making more mistakes and gives weaker answers than before. Expected result: If temporary fallback is necessary because GPT-5.4 is unavailable or saturated, the product should automatically return to GPT-5.4 as soon as it is available again. At minimum, there should be a strict model lock option, or the UI should clearly indicate that fallback occurred and that the conversation is no longer using the manually selected model. Why this is a problem: I explicitly chose GPT-5.4 because I want that quality level. If the product silently downgrades and keeps the conversation on another model, manual model selection becomes unreliable and misleading. Additional notes: - I understand temporary fallback may be necessary. - My complaint is that it does not return to the manually selected model afterwards. - This creates a visible drop in quality and hurts trust in the model selector. - Please add either: 1. a strict "lock selected model" option, or 2. automatic return to the user-selected model after temporary fallback, 3. and explicit UI disclosure when fallback happens. This is not just a preference issue. The fallback appears persistent and materially changes answer quality within the same conversation. title: Export Chat truncates file to 0 bytes when disk is full instead of failing gracefully
body:
When exporting a chat session via Ctrl+Shift+P > "Chat: Export Session", if the disk is full, the extension truncates the target file to 0 bytes and then fails to write the content. The result is permanent data loss -- the file ends up empty with no error message or recovery option.

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Fill the root partition to 100% (or near 100% so the export file cannot fit)
2. Open a Copilot Chat session with substantial conversation history
3. Run Ctrl+Shift+P > "Chat: Export Session"
4. Choose a file path on the full partition (e.g. overwrite an existing JSON export)
5. Observe the resulting file is 0 bytes -- all original content destroyed

Expected Behavior:
The export should either:
1. Check available disk space before writing, or
2. Write to a temporary file first, then atomically rename it to the target path (so the original file is never destroyed on failure), or
3. At minimum, show a clear error message and not truncate the existing file

Actual Behavior:
The file is opened with truncation (write mode), the write fails due to ENOSPC, and the user is left with a 0-byte file. No error dialog appears. Original content is irrecoverably lost.

Environment:
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04, Linux
- Filesystem: ext4, root partition at 100% usage (0 bytes available)

This is especially problematic because the user may be trying to export the chat session precisely because they are worried about losing context -- and the export itself destroys their previous backup. The fix is straightforward: use atomic write (write to temp file + rename) which is a standard pattern for safe file writes.

title: Feature Request: Add a setting to configure the default agent (Agent/Plan/Ask) for new chat sessions
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

## Feature Request

Currently, new Copilot Chat sessions always default to the **Agent** agent. There is no user-configurable setting to change this default. Users who primarily work with the **Plan** or **Ask** agent must manually switch the agent picker at the start of every new chat session.

### Proposal

Add a setting (e.g. `chat.defaultMode` or similar) that allows users to choose which built-in agent (Agent, Plan, or Ask) is selected by default when opening a new chat session.

**Example:**
```json
{
  "chat.defaultMode": "plan"
}
```

Accepted values could be `"agent"`, `"plan"`, `"ask"`, or the identifier of a custom agent.

### Use Case

Different teams and individuals have different workflows. Some prefer a plan-first approach where they review a structured implementation plan before any code changes are made. Others may primarily use Ask for research and exploration. Being able to set the default agent per workspace (via `.vscode/settings.json`) would allow teams to optimize for their preferred workflow without the friction of manually switching the agent on every new session.

### Current Workaround

- Manually selecting Plan from the agent picker each time a new chat session is started.
- Using the `vscode://GitHub.Copilot-Chat/chat?mode=plan` URL scheme, which is not practical for everyday use.

### Environment

- VS Code Version: 1.114.0
- OS: macOS (arm64)
- Copilot Chat Extension: 0.42.x

title: Multiple instance of VS code is loaded when enabling powershell as default terminal in Windows
body:
Type: Bug I have default terminal set to PowerShell (pwsh) terminal.integrated.defaultProfile.windows: Powershell After this Multiple instance of VSCode is opened automatically. Reported the same issue ([299416](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/299416)) with earlier version as well, but it got closed. Still Experiencing the same issue, even when the Copilot agent opens any pwsh commands it auto opens new VSCode instance. PFA Screenshot. NOTE: If I set "Command Prompt" then its working fine - for better terminal integration switched to Powershell - which is causing the issue. $PROFILE ----------- C:\Users\USERNAME\Documents\PowerShell\Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1 ------------ ```ps1 # https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/terminal/shell-integration #if ($env:TERM_PROGRAM -eq "vscode") { .
